newsitem.title: USA: Exporter pleads guilty to cheating USDA on DEIP.
newsitem.headline: Exporter pleads guilty to cheating USDA on DEIP.

text.p: Harjit Singh, a Florida exporter, pleaded guilty in U.S. district court to charges of defrauding the Agriculture Department of $1 million in dairy export contracts, U.S. attorney Eric Holder said Friday.

According to Holder, Singh won eight contracts under the Dairy Export Incentive Program for export of dry milk powder during 1993 to a company allegedly based in Dubai. Instead, the powder was sold through disguised transactions to a firm in the Philippines, which were not a DEIP target country.
Singh, of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, is president of two export firms, Milk Maid Inc and MMI International Corp.
Overall, Holder said, the scheme netted Singh's companies $1,018,679 in export subsidy payments.
At present, Singh and his companies are suspended from participating in federal contracting programs.
Sentencing was set for January 15. Maximum penalty for Singh would be five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
